subject: Starlight RFP: Admin lifecycle, approval matrix, and escalation workflows
messages:

Cc: Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@starlight.com>

Subject: RFP Q: admin lifecycle + emergency escalation flows

Ben — thanks for the packet last week. A couple of clarifications from our security/compliance team as we map requirements into our procurement matrix:

1) Approval matrix: can Redwood support a two-stage approval for privileged role elevation (request -> manager approval -> security approver) and enforce time-boxed elevations (e.g., 4 hours max) with automated rollback?

2) Break-glass / emergency accounts: does Redwood provide a separate auditable break-glass path that bypasses normal SSO provisioning but still creates immutable audit trails?

3) SCIM sync: we rely on delta syncs and user attribute-driven role mapping. Are there size limits for bulk re-provisioning, and how do you handle concurrent attribute updates during sync windows?

We'd like short answers plus any example artifacts you can share ahead of the technical call.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, IT Security
Starlight Inc.

Hi Elena — great questions, appreciate the specificity. High level answers below and I attached two artifacts: an approval matrix PDF and a SCIM delta patterns workbook. I'll let Kimberly and Marissa add technical detail where helpful.

1) Two-stage approvals & time-boxed elevations: yes. Redwood supports configurable, multi-step approval workflows. You can chain approvers (manager -> security approver) and assign TTLs to temporary role grants. When TTL expires the grant is automatically revoked and a system event is logged. We also expose webhook and audit hooks so you can automate rollback if downstream checks fail.

2) Break-glass accounts: we support break-glass escalation paths that are off-band from normal SSO flows. Break-glass activations require multi-party approval (can be configured), are routed to a separate audit ledger, and produce immutable events including requestor, why, and an attached justification artifact. Access tokens issued for break-glass are marked and time-limited.

3) SCIM delta syncs: our SCIM service supports incremental (delta) sync with per-tenant configurable bulk windows. Typical throughput supports up to 50k user ops per minute in Dedicated capacity; for very large directories we recommend staggered shard syncs and we provide a resume token to reconcile interrupted updates. Concurrency: we use last-write-wins with operation timestamps and provide pre- and post-sync dry-run mode to detect mapping conflicts.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical deep dive with Kimberly (security architect) and Marissa (SSO/SCIM specialist). Available windows tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT or Tue 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Elena — adding technical specifics on SSO, token marking, and audit integration.

- SAML/OIDC behavior: both SAML assertions and OIDC ID tokens can carry an elevation claim. For temporary elevations we emit a separate session token with an "elevated_until" claim; this token is short-lived and logged to the audit stream. We also support step-up authentication (MFA prompt) as part of the approval flow.

- Token provenance & immutable audit: all elevation events are written to our append-only audit store and exported to customer-managed logging (S3/Cloud Storage or syslog). Break-glass events are tagged with an immutable ECC-signed token id so tampering is detectable.

- Approvals API & automation: approvals can be collected via UI, email-to-approve links, or programmatic Approval API. Approvals consumed by the system include approver id, decision, TTL, and optional justification. Approver delegation is supported with explicit delegation grants and expiry.

I'll prepare a short diagram for the call showing runtime token flows and audit exports.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Elena — wanted to add SCIM and RBAC mapping details you asked about:

- Attribute-driven RBAC: Redwood maps incoming SCIM attributes (groups, custom claims) to internal roles via a rules engine. Rules are evaluated in order; you can set precedence, and we support regex-based attribute matching for flexible mapping.

- Delta vs full sync: delta is default. For large imports or attribute-normalization jobs we support a controlled full-sync mode (snapshot -> reconcile) with a dry-run preview. Bulk re-provisioning is throttled and checkpointed; we emit progress events you can monitor.

- Concurrent updates: SCIM operations include an "externalVersion" field; when enabled we perform optimistic concurrency checks and surface conflicts to the admin UI and audit logs for manual resolution. If you prefer transactional semantics, we can propose a blue/green provisioning approach for tenant-heavy migrations.

- Example playbook: request elevation -> manager approval -> security approval -> system issues elevated session token with TTL -> scheduled revocation job validates and revokes at TTL -> final audit record generated. We included the playbook steps in the attached PDF (page 4).

Happy to review the playbook live on the call.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
